# 2 Chronicles Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Then Solomon declared, "The LORD has said He would dwell in a dark cloud.

**2** I have built You a magnificent temple, a place for You to live forever."

**3** Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel as they stood there.

**4** He said, "Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who has fulfilled with His hands what He promised with His mouth to my father David.

**5** He said, 'From the day I brought My people out of Egypt, I did not choose any city in all the tribes of Israel for a temple to bear My name, and I did not choose anyone to be ruler over My people Israel.

**6** But now I have chosen Jerusalem for My name to dwell there, and I have chosen David to rule My people Israel.'

**7** My father David had it in his heart to build a temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**8** But the LORD said to my father David, 'You did well to have it in your heart to build a temple for My name.

**9** Nevertheless, you are not the one to build it. Instead, your own son will build the temple for My name.'

**10** The LORD has kept the promise He made. I have succeeded my father David and sit on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised, and I have built the temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

**11** There I have placed the ark containing the covenant the LORD made with the people of Israel."

**12** Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the entire assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.

**13** (Solomon had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and placed it in the center of the outer court.) He stood on it, then knelt before the whole assembly of Israel and stretched his hands toward heaven.

**14** He prayed: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven or on earth — You who keep Your covenant of love with Your servants who walk wholeheartedly before You.

**15** You have kept Your promise to Your servant David my father. What You said with Your mouth, You have fulfilled with Your hand — as we see today.

**16** Now, LORD, God of Israel, keep the other promise You made to Your servant David my father: 'You will never fail to have a man sitting before Me on the throne of Israel, if only your descendants are careful to walk in My law as you have walked before Me.'

**17** Now, LORD, God of Israel, let Your promise to Your servant David come true.

**18** "But will God really live on earth with humans? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You — how much less this temple I have built!

**19** Yet give attention to Your servant's prayer and his plea for mercy, LORD my God. Hear the cry and the prayer Your servant is praying in Your presence.

**20** May Your eyes be open toward this temple day and night — this place of which You said, 'My name shall be there' — so that You will hear the prayer Your servant prays toward this place.

**21** Hear the prayers of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, Your dwelling place, and when You hear, forgive.

**22** "When someone wrongs their neighbor and is required to take an oath and comes to swear before Your altar in this temple,

**23** then hear from heaven and act. Judge between Your servants, punishing the guilty and bringing down on their heads what they have done, and vindicating the innocent by treating them as their righteousness deserves.

**24** "When Your people Israel are defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against You, and when they turn back and acknowledge Your name, praying and making supplication before You in this temple,

**25** then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land You gave them and their ancestors.

**26** "When the heavens are shut and there is no rain because Your people have sinned against You, and when they pray toward this place and acknowledge Your name and turn from their sin because You have afflicted them,

**27** then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land You gave Your people as their inheritance.

**28** "When famine or plague comes to the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, or when an enemy besieges them in any of their cities — whatever disaster or disease may come —

**29** when a prayer or plea is made by anyone among Your people Israel, each one aware of their own afflictions and pains and spreading out their hands toward this temple —

**30** then hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. Forgive and deal with everyone according to all they do, since You know their hearts (for You alone know every human heart),

**31** so that they will fear You and walk in Your ways all the days they live in the land You gave our ancestors.

**32** "As for the foreigner who does not belong to Your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your outstretched arm — when they come and pray toward this temple,

**33** then hear from heaven, Your dwelling place. Do whatever the foreigner asks of You, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name and fear You, as Your own people Israel do, and may know that this house I have built bears Your name.

**34** "When Your people go to war against their enemies, wherever You send them, and they pray to You toward this city You have chosen and the temple I have built for Your name,

**35** then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.

**36** "When they sin against You — and who doesn't sin? — and You become angry with them and give them over to their enemies, who carry them off to a land far away or nearby,

**37** and if they have a change of heart in the land where they are held captive, and repent and plead with You in the land of their captivity and say, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'

**38** and if they turn back to You with all their heart and soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray toward the land You gave their ancestors, toward the city You have chosen, and toward the temple I have built for Your name,

**39** then from heaven, Your dwelling place, hear their prayer and their pleas, and uphold their cause. And forgive Your people, who have sinned against You.

**40** "Now, my God, may Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.

**41** "Now arise, LORD God, and come to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your might. May Your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may Your faithful people rejoice in Your goodness.

**42** LORD God, do not reject Your anointed one. Remember the great love promised to David Your servant."


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **6:18**: "Will God really live on earth with humans?" — This is the most important question in the chapter. Solomon knows the answer is both no and yes. God cannot be contained, but He chooses to be present.

- **6:32-33**: The prayer for foreigners is remarkable. Solomon envisions the temple as a place where non-Israelites encounter God — and asks God to answer their prayers too. This is missionary theology embedded in architecture.

- **6:36**: "Who doesn't sin?" — Solomon builds the entire prayer structure on the assumption of failure. The temple isn't designed for perfect people. It's designed for people who will fail and need a way back.

- **6:42**: The prayer ends not with Solomon's name but with David's. Everything about this temple ultimately rests on God's promises to David — not on Solomon's achievement.


— PNEUMA
